story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Blackhawks (7-14-2) beat Calgary 4-3 in overtime last night, and the Canucks (6-18-1) beat Minnesota 4-3 in a shootout the same night. Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (tied for 29th in the NHL) and the Canucks are last in the NHL.

The Blackhawks’ record (.348) is about what their chances are worth. The Canucks haven’t played well, but their record (.260) is worse than their play: their chances are worth about .326, and their goaltending has held them back.

The Blackhawks pick their shots (lowest), have struggled on the power play (32nd) and don’t block many shots (31st). Chicago has scored 2.52 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league, and allowed 4.00, the second most. On the other side, the Canucks have had shaky goaltending (32nd), have a leaky penalty kill (32nd) and ice the puck a lot (31st). Vancouver has allowed 4.32 goals a game, the most in the league. The Canucks have the edge over the Blackhawks on physicality.

Sam Rinzel (2 G / 15 A / 17 P in 22 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, with twelve points in his last five games. Frank Nazar (11 G / 3 A / 14 P in 21 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, with seven points in his last five games. The Canucks’ scoring runs through Brock Boeser (8 G / 19 A / 27 P in 25 GP), who has ten points in his last five games.
Drew Commesso is expected to start for Chicago, his first start of the season, and Nikita Tolopilo (1-0-0 / .944 SV% in 1 GS) for Vancouver.
